Last week I finally acquired a spot to garden. I am currently back in school, at a university that happens to have Agriculture in the title, and it's been impossible to find a community garden project through the horticulture department. I even worked with the VP of a student life club that donates food to local food banks and shelters to try and acquire a place to plant my vegetable garden, but nothing worked out. I spent almost 2 semesters trying to find some space. My apartment complex is completely out of the question.

Flip forward to July. Outside of the building where I am working on an internship there is an 18x18 raised bed in the parking lot that has been mostly abandoned aside from a fig tree and two small orange trees my boss planted years ago.

I just recieved permission to plant there and I am so happy. A few days ago I prepped a small area, and next week my boss' nephew is going to pick up a few cubic yards of compost for me to add to the sad dirt that's there.

I already put Giant Mayan Corn seeds in the ground, with some King Of The Garden Lima beans to climb them, a small cilantro patch, and 4 basil plants.

I am in the process of germinating chili seeds, pumpkin seeds, melon seeds and noodle bean seeds I brought back from Myanmar and Laos last summer, as well as ocra, brandywine and cherry tomatoes, habañero peppers, albino pumpkins, and a few watermelons.

If I am lucky, I'll be able to have a short harvest from mid October to late November here in S.E. United States.

I realize it's a little late, but I'm really happy I get to have a garden for the 5 months before I graduate!

I have been taking pictures on the slow transformation and I'll post them after I finally get some veggies.

If there is anyone in the Baton Rouge/New Orleans area that knows a nursery or garden center that actually still has decent looking herb or vegetables let me know!
